headline: White House seeks to limit information contractors should share with Congress
author: Dhruti Shah

paragraphs.text: Donald Trump has issued an executive order ordering federal contractors to inform the White House about any congressional requests for information about their work with the government, and withhold any information the government considers confidential or protected by executive privilege.

It is the White House’s latest move pushing back against congressional oversight as it prepares itself for an aggressive fight against planned investigations from a Congress that will be led by Democrats in January.

Friday’s order said that “certain congressional leaders” had been “seeking confidential executive branch information from agencies and harassing private companies that contract with the Federal Government.”
Contractors who fail to comply with these requirements could see their existing contracts canceled and potentially be barred from future federal work, said the order, which was issued late Friday.

“The executive branch must be able to work closely with its employees and contractors on sensitive matters without fear that confidential information will be released to unauthorized third parties,” the order added.

Legal experts have previously told The Post they expect the issue of whether the Trump administration’s communications with outside figures could be covered by executive privilege to be fiercely debated, and likely to wind up being tested in court.

The White House has taken several steps to prepare for clashes with Democrats over congressional oversight and legislative probes next year. Meanwhile, private companies have been scrambling to prepare for subpoenas as the next Congress is expected to focus more than usual on the private sector and companies that had dealings with the Trump administration.
On Monday, White House counsel Will Scharf issued an internal directive requiring federal agencies to seek White House approval before any personnel testify before Congress.

And on Nov. 11, the White House released a letter from Scharf to Rep. Robert Garcia (D-California), who is expected to chair the House Oversight Committee in the new Congress. That letter accused Democrats of “abusive and capricious threats” and said the administration would resist congressional subpoenas on the grounds that they lack a “legitimate legislative purpose.”
Garcia described the letter as an intimidation tactic, telling The Post: “We’re not going to be intimidated, and the president’s not going to stop us from investigation.”
